borderline.why: The Act is read and carries no newcomer provision, but the entry hedges twice - the definition 'was located' in no source, and the three parallel public systems are said to 'shift the question' rather than settle it.
Denies a newcomer designation, yet describes placement by English proficiency band (Emerging, Stage 1, Stages 2-4), which is a proficiency placement pupils progress out of.
Says no EAL designation 'was found' and that the SEN policy carrying the only relevant rule was never retrieved, so the absence rests entirely on a secondary summary.
The whole basis is that Eurydice records no newcomer criterion, which is silence in a comparative source rather than a finding that no category exists.
Opens with the not-established sentinel but then states that Lei 17/16 'creates no newcomer or second-language pupil category' - the sentinel and the body disagree.
No criterion is stated in any of three sources, but the same entry records that Bosnia and Herzegovina is outside several Eurydice figures entirely, so the silence may be coverage.
The only source read is the Grade 1 Language Arts curriculum, too narrow to establish that no designation exists anywhere in Bahamian policy.

The Education Code defines no newcomer category, yet the entry names a newcomer-facing rule - exemption from Belarusian or Russian study for foreign citizens temporarily present - which is a status pupils can leave.
Bare absence in a single PEER profile whose language section is said to cover minority access rather than language, with CAR outside PASEC2019 and ELAN-Afrique too.
The term counts are taken from PEIB, the indigenous-education programme, not from Chile's education law, so 'migrante 0' is absence in a document where it would be absent anyway.
One line of bare absence in a single PEER inclusion profile, with no medium-of-instruction or cohort reasoning to support it.
No designation 'was found', but the entry says migrant provision sits with an intercultural education department it calls unverifiable here.
Bare absence in the PEER profile plus a note that Djibouti is in neither PASEC2019 nor the ELAN-Afrique list, so nothing positive supports the absence.
A single line saying no designation 'was found in any retrieved Dominican source' - a statement about retrieval, with no instrument named as read.
No designation 'was found in any Grenadian source' and the PEER profile has no language section at all, so both the search and the source come up empty.
The first line says no category exists in the Law, but the second names a trigger - citizenship plus a native language other than Georgian - which is a designation on a non-proficiency basis.
Denies an arrival-based category while saying the inclusion framework 'indexes linguistic difference', which may itself be a language-based grouping.
The absence rests on a profile whose linguistic-groups section the entry says is two sentences long in total.
Never states that no designation exists; it establishes only that the 2001 bilingual-education policy was never adopted and that the question is a home variety.
The finding is 0 hits in two cited chapters, while the same entry records a large Syrian arrival cohort - a population where a designation would be expected if one existed.
Term counts are zero, but the entry says the review is 2,589 characters and covers no support measures, which is too thin to establish anything.
The entry disqualifies its own finding: 'alolingv' 0 hits is in a timetable document, and it says so - 'absence here is weaker than absence in an act'.
A single hedged line - 'No newcomer category was found in the sources read' - with no instrument, term count or cohort reasoning behind it.
Opens with the not-established sentinel but the body says the curriculum framework treats English and French as whole-cohort targets 'rather than designating a subgroup of second-language pupils'.
PEER records no designation, but the entry closes by saying nothing was found on displaced or South Sudanese children - exactly the population where a designation would arise.
The Act creates no such category, but its s.10 list of pupils entitled to specially provided education includes communication deficiencies, which may or may not reach language.
Absence in the PEER profile, which the entry says carries no medium-of-instruction statement at all, so there is no positive whole-cohort rule behind the absence.
Opens with the not-established sentinel but then states there is no newcomer or second-language category in either cited source, with 0 hits in PP-1875.
No designation 'was found in any Vincentian source' and the only retrievable language provision is the regional OECS curriculum, not a national instrument.
The Law creates no designation and addresses ethnic minority people as a group, but it explicitly leaves provision to separate Government regulations that were not read.
